problem:
A stone of mass $15\,\text{kg}$ falls vertically downward. Let $v$ be its velocity, with downward taken as the positive direction.
The air resistance on the stone is proportional to the square of its velocity with a constant of proportionality $k=2\,\text{kg/m}$ and acts opposite to the direction of motion.

What is the terminal velocity ${v}_{\text{term}}$ of the stone? Assume the acceleration due to gravity is $g=9.8\,{\text{m/s}}^{2},$ and the only forces acting on the stone are the weight due to gravity and drag.

Express your answer in the form $a\sqrt{b},$ where $a$ and $b$ are rational numbers.

${v}_{\text{term}}=$
{{field-1}}
$\text{m/s}$
